overall_notes: Solid slate with 6/8 legs meeting break-even thresholds; two cuts justified by fundamental disconnect between historical rates and market pricing (L2) and high personnel-driven uncertainty (L8). NFLprices are stale (Sat 9 AM) and single-book NBA pricing inflates est_probs, so treat upper bounds as ceiling.

votes.reasoning: Geno Smith under 1.5 passes a clean filter: 67% historical hit rate, 64.3% est_prob, and 0 TDs last week at KC support the under. Trailing script (−8.5 dogs) raises attempts but this offense struggles to finish drives. Risk: Garrett Wilson Q but expected (cleared concussion), which could improve red-zone access. Edge is clear vs. break-even.

Dak Prescott over 1.5 fails the smell test: only 44% historical hit rate (4/9 games) but market is betting 62.5% over, a 18-point gap. Last week's 2 TDs on 335 yards despite volume shows efficiency hasn't risen. Loss of Jake Ferguson (TE, red-zone target) removes a key threat. Dome and trailing script (−4.5 favorites) explain market overvaluation, but data doesn't support the over.

Blake Corum under 1.5 receptions anchors on 62.5% hit rate (5/8) matching 61.4% est_prob—a sharp 1.5% hold pair signals market efficiency. Zero catches in last two games + early-down role lock in the baseline. Risk: Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on IR create target redistribution; short-passing game could flow to Corum. This is real uncertainty but doesn't override the baseline.

Cooper Kupp under 2.5 receptions has 67% historical rate (6/9) exceeding 59.4% est_prob, a modest 7.6% edge. Sam Darnold (quad) out, Drew Lock starting, should depress overall passing volume + SEA −6.5 favorites drives run-heavy scheme. Risk: Lock is an unknown; game could devolve into chaos, and JSN may absorb the target distribution shift unpredictably. Borderline confidence due to QB chaos.

Trevor Lawrence over 1.5 TDs: 62.5% historical hit rate (5/8) exceeds 59.7% est_prob by 3%, and TEN LBs Cody Barton + Anthony Hill Jr. out is a meaningful edge (reduced pressure). JAX −10.5 favorites could suppress late attempts, but the TD theorem doesn't hinge on volume. Recent form (4/0/3/1/2/4/3/1 TDs) shows volatility but upside present.

Michael Penix Jr. under 1.5 TDs is a strong edge play: 71% historical hit rate (5/7) crushes 58.2% est_prob by +13 points—a significant market inefficiency. ATL is Bijan-centric (run-heavy), Zachariah Branch (WR) out further caps passing threats. KC −3 low total (47) supports a defensive grind. Conviction is high here.

OG Anunoby under 2.5 threes is marginal: 60% historical hit rate nearly matches 62.9% est_prob, but single-book (FanDuel) pricing inflates the estimate; true prob ~61%, barely above 60% baseline. NYK back-to-back (played IND Saturday) introduces fatigue / rest risk. This is close to break-even and depends entirely on whether B2B load impacts his minutes.

Jabari Smith Jr. under 2.5 threes deteriorates under personnel scrutiny: VanVleet (out), Capela (out), Smart (suspended) create massive role uncertainty. While last 5 games all ≤2 makes is a recent trend, sample is tiny. HOU back-to-back (at UTAH Saturday) could fatigue him or expand role unpredictably. Single-book (FanDuel) pricing inflates 62.9% est_prob; drafter flags low confidence. Chaos premium too high.
